feed.title: NPR Programs: All Things Considered
feed.subtitle: All Things Considered hosts Ailsa Chang, Mary Louise Kelly, Juana Summers and Scott Detrow present the program's trademark mix of news, interviews, commentaries, reviews, and offbeat features 7 days a week.

entry.title: Solar micro grids going up in North Carolina to help storm prep
entry.summary: Solar microgrids are helping Western North Carolina to prepare for disasters like hurricane Helene, which devastated the region two years ago.

entry.title: The federal law aimed at protecting college students from sexual abuse
entry.summary: The lawsuit by a former Cornell University student, alleging she was raped in 2024 by seven male students, has renewed long-standing concerns about how colleges deal with sexual assault.

entry.title: New novel shows what can happen when a megachurch pastor's wife questions everything
entry.summary: NPR's Juana Summers talks with author Deesha Philyaw about her debut novel, "The True Confessions of First Lady Freeman."

entry.title: The race to protect Santa Rosa Island's rare, damaged Torrey pines
entry.summary: In May, a fire damaged 80% of the trees one of the only two naturally-occurring groves of Torrey Pines in the world. The National Park Service is trying to help them recover.

entry.title: How President Trump's memo on domestic terrorism has targeted left-leaning protests
entry.summary: NPR's Sacha Pfeiffer speaks with the Brennan Center's Faiza Patel about the year since President Trump issued National Security Presidential Memorandum 7.

entry.title: Trump hosts tech executives as administration doubles down on AI
entry.summary: President Trump met with AI CEOs at the White House on Tuesday and promoted a new government AI tool even as concerns about the technology's risks grow.

entry.title: Anger mounts over Cornell's response to student's sexual assault allegations
entry.summary: Prosecutors have reopened an investigation into the alleged rape of a former Cornell University student in 2024. Now the governor of New York is calling for an independent investigation into Cornell.

entry.title: Guitarist Tom Morello gets political on 'Everyone Gets Everything They Want'
entry.summary: NPR's Juana Summers talks with Tom Morello, co-founder of Rage Against the Machine, about his first solo rock record Everyone Gets Everything They Want.

entry.title: Judge considers motions in Lindsay Clancy's case
entry.summary: A judge heard statements on several motions, including one to dismiss the case of Lindsay Clancy, after her recent trial ended in mistrial.

entry.title: Historic science museum in Philadelphia to close
entry.summary: Philadelphia's Academy of Natural Sciences is set to close down thanks to financial pressures. The 198-year-old museum houses important scientific specimens and a beloved dinosaur exhibit.
